title: Read a config from any reader
description:
Write the core of a config loader that works on anything implementing `BufRead` (a file, standard input, or a string in tests):

- `fn parse_config<R: BufRead>(reader: R) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, ConfigError>` reads `key = value` lines. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped; keys and values are trimmed.
- `enum ConfigError { Io(std::io::Error), Syntax { line: usize, text: String }, Duplicate { line: usize, key: String } }` with `impl Display` giving `"read error: <e>"`, `"line <n>: expected key = value, got <text>"` and `"line <n>: <key> is set twice"`. Line numbers count from 1.
- `impl From<std::io::Error> for ConfigError`, so `?` converts read errors.
- `fn load_or_default(path: &str) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, ConfigError>` opens the file with `BufReader`; a file that does not exist (`ErrorKind::NotFound`) gives an empty map instead of an error.
hints: `std::io::Cursor::new(text)` turns a string into something that implements `BufRead`, which is how the tests feed `parse_config` without any file. Write the function against the trait, and it works for files too.
`reader.lines().enumerate()` gives each line with its index (from 0); each line is itself a `Result`, and `line?` uses your `From` impl to turn an `io::Error` into `ConfigError::Io`.
